key_insight: Plastic slip in FCC crystals is controlled less by stress alone and more by the supply of long dislocation links, whose length distribution strongly shapes the shear rate.
engineering_relevance: This provides a physically grounded slip-law for crystal plasticity models, improving prediction of orientation-dependent plastic flow in metals.
method: Integrate shear-rate contributions from dislocation links over link length on each slip system.
Use a generalized Orowan relation with link density n_i(l) and average link velocity v_i(l).
Model v_i(l) with a unified function of resolved shear stress and link length across all slip systems.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces DDD shear-rate data for all 12 FCC slip systems across 99 loading orientations and explains the observed exponential stress dependence without thermal activation.
watch_item: Because slip activity is highly sensitive to the long-link tail of n_i(l), the model may require careful calibration of link-length statistics in different microstructures.
paper_title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
